intended_object: The i-th root subgroup homomorphism x_i : 𝔾ₐ(A) → G(A) on A-points, for every commutative ring A. Here G is the "toral Kostant closure", a closed subgroup scheme of GLₙ over ℤ given by a quotient Hopf algebra. This is the Chevalley-style map t ↦ exp(t·ρ(e_i)) (Carter §4.4). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body applies the functor of points (`CommHopfAlgCat.Hom.mapPointsFunctor`) to the Hopf algebra morphism `kostantRootSubgroupToralCoordinateMap`, which goes from the quotient Hopf algebra of `GLₙ` to the coordinate Hopf algebra of `𝔾ₐ`, and evaluates at `A`. Because the functor of points is contravariant, this gives a group homomorphism 𝔾ₐ(A) → G(A). This is the standard way a map of affine group schemes is defined from its comorphism. Lemmas in the same file confirm the intended meaning. Including the result into GLₙ(A) gives back the original root-subgroup point. In matrix form it is the divided-power exponential `kostantRootSubgroupMatrix`. Working over ℤ for every commutative ring A is the natural setting for Chevalley group schemes, and the ℚ-Lie algebra setting is needed for the Kostant ℤ-form. It is a specific construction, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no counterpart for Chevalley root subgroups.
